title_zh: MacroVoices #549 Matt Barrie（Freelancer.com CEO）：AI-gent Provocateur（AI 智能体的挑衅者）
subtitle_zh: Matt Barrie 讲述 agentic AI 落地、开源模型经济学与白领岗位大重构。
summary_zh: 本期 MacroVoices（第 549 期）由 Eric Townsend 与 Patrick Ceresna 对话 Freelancer.com CEO、被称「人工智能先生」的 Matt Barrie，主题是 agentic AI（智能体式 AI）的落地。Barrie 说自己近一个月被 AI 与 agent 的能力「red-pill」（大开眼界）：如今已能相当可靠地自动化公司里的日常工作流，甚至比人更快更强。他现身说法——自己搭了约 44 个 agent 处理琐事：把原本需 11 人 24 小时轮班的项目审核「队列处理」（queue processing）用两三次会话就自动化；一名六位数薪水、每天重复调 Google Ads 旋钮的效果营销员工离职后，他让 agent 每天综合 Analytics、广告账户、数据库、财务与工单系统，早上把调整建议发到邮箱，做得比人更好。他判断 AI 里所有传统护城河都死了——相关科学基本发表在约 40 篇技术论文里；开源（尤其中国模型）看起来在赢，因为可在自有硬件上无限使用，但要为此接受能力上的降级。他算过一笔能源账：若人人每天烧 40 亿 token，需要约 30 太瓦（terawatt），约为当今世界能源产量的 10 倍，远超在建数据中心规模，故 token 消耗注定不会免费。他还预言一场「创业大爆炸」，让人像创意总监而非推像素般思考。

turns.en: And if you think about the scale of 1.65 trillion in debt in five years, you know, subprime peaked at 1.3 trillion in 2007. And that, that was had 55 million mortgages behind it.
turns.zh: 想想看，五年内 1.65 万亿美元的债务规模——2007 年次贷峰值也才 1.3 万亿美元，而次贷背后是 5500 万笔房贷。

turns.en: Well, this AI explosion has two customers open AI on the therapy. That was freelancer.com CEO and artificial intelligence expert, Matt Berry.
turns.zh: 而这轮 AI 爆炸只有两个客户：OpenAI 和 Anthropic。刚才说话的是 Freelancer.com CEO、人工智能专家 Matt Barrie。

turns.en: I'm Eric Townsend. And this is macro voices, the free weekly podcast targeting professional finance and sophisticated private investors. Episode 549 was produced on September 10th, 2026.
turns.zh: 我是 Eric Townsend。这里是 Macro Voices，一档面向专业金融人士和成熟个人投资者的免费周更播客。第 549 期制作于 2026 年 9 月 10 日。

turns.en: The artificial intelligence arms race is really taking off and the pace is accelerating and the stakes have never been higher. Freelancer.com CEO Matt Berry needs little introduction to our longtime macro voices listeners. And this might be his best AI interview yet.
turns.zh: 人工智能军备竞赛正在真正起飞，节奏越来越快，赌注也前所未有地高。对我们 Macro Voices 的老听众来说，Freelancer.com 的 CEO Matt Barrie 已经不需要多做介绍。这可能是他至今最精彩的一次 AI 访谈。

turns.en: So make some popcorn, sit back and get ready. I intentionally let this one run long because the subject matter is so important. Matt also produced another of his famous missives on the subject of AI.
turns.zh: 所以爆点爆米花，坐下来准备好。我特意让这一期做得长一些，因为话题实在太重要。Matt 还就 AI 主题写下了他另一篇著名长文（missive）。

turns.en: And you'll find that LinkedIn, your research roundup email. The difference this time around versus previous interviews is that in the past, we covered the actual content of the writing in the interview.
turns.zh: 你会在 LinkedIn、以及你的 research roundup 邮件里找到那篇文章。这一次和以往不同的地方在于，过去我们是在访谈里直接聊那篇文章的内容。

turns.en: This time they're two separate pieces, giving you a double dose of Matt Berry on AI. So listen in here for the audio, then download and read his latest piece, which is LinkedIn, your research roundup.
turns.zh: 这次是两个独立的作品，让你 double dose 一次听够 Matt Barrie 谈 AI。所以先在这里听音频，然后去下载阅读他的最新文章——在 LinkedIn 和你的 research roundup 邮件里。

turns.en: And I'm Patrick Suresna. Let's dive into this interview. Joining me now is Freelancer.com CEO and founder, Matt Berry. Very well known to our audience as Mr. Artificial Intelligence.
turns.zh: 我是 Patrick Ceresna。让我们进入今天的访谈。现在加入我们的是 Freelancer.com 的 CEO 兼创始人 Matt Barrie。我们的听众都非常熟悉他，人称"人工智能先生"。

turns.en: Matt, I want to start with just an update. So much is changing in the world of AI. Since the last time that I spoke to you and interviewed you here on macro voices, I'd say probably the biggest thing is agentic AI.
turns.zh: Matt，我想先请你做个近况更新。AI 世界变化太快了。自从上次我在 Macro Voices 采访你之后，我想最大的变化应该就是 agentic AI（智能体式 AI）。

turns.en: I think really understanding what that means takes some understanding. So put it in perspective for us. Thanks, Eric. Thanks for having me. I've been totally red-pilled in the last month or so from what you can do now with AI and agents. What I mean by this, I think AI has reached the point where now you can quite reliably get it to do workflows, which means that you really now have an ability to take something that someone
turns.zh: 我想真正理解它到底意味着什么需要一些背景。请你给我们讲讲。谢谢 Eric，感谢邀请。过去一个月左右，我彻底被 AI 和 agent 现在能做的事情"red-pill"（大开眼界）了。我的意思是，AI 已经达到了这样一个阶段——你可以相当可靠地让它执行工作流（workflows），也就是说你现在真的能把某个

turns.en: in your company might be doing as part of their daily job and automate that in a very reliable way at greater than human capability in many circumstances and very quickly and very efficiently.
turns.zh: 你公司里某个员工日常要做的事情拿出来，用一种非常可靠的方式自动化，而且在很多情况下比人的能力更强、更快、更高效。

turns.en: So to give you a concrete example of the sorts of things that I've been doing, I currently have about 40 agents, 44, I think, last night, agents in my fleet that I personally put together to do various bits and pieces.
turns.zh: 给你举个我自己一直在做的具体例子：我目前大概有 40 个 agent，昨晚数了一下应该是 44 个——都是我自己搭起来的 agent 队伍，用来处理各种各样的琐事。

turns.en: I can look at a team and quite a number of teams in large companies have workflows. So one might be queue processing. Every day, projects come into Freelancer.com, posted from the world, and it's free to post a project.
turns.zh: 我会去看一个团队——大公司里相当多的团队都有工作流。其中一种就是队列处理（queue processing）。每天都有来自世界各地的项目在 Freelancer.com 上发布，发项目是免费的。

turns.en: We do have a statistical classifier that kind of runs over those projects to determine whether they're good or bad. But sometimes a statistical classifier doesn't really know the answer to whether the product is good or bad and will escalate it to a human to review.
turns.zh: 我们确实有一个统计分类器会过一遍这些项目，判断好坏。但有时候统计分类器其实并不知道这个项目到底是好是坏，就会把它升级给人类来审核。

turns.en: And so there's a team of people that 24 by 7 will go into that queue, look over projects, look over their provenance, look through a whole bunch of metadata related to the user, et cetera, and so forth and make a decision on whether to approve that project or not.
turns.zh: 所以我们有一支 24 小时轮班的团队，进入这个队列，审视项目、审视项目的来源、翻看和用户相关的一整套元数据等等，然后决定是否批准这个项目。

turns.en: Now, to get 24 by 7 operation, I need about 11 people in that team and they don't just process the projects. They also deal with violations that are reported on projects that are posted and contest and a range of other things.
turns.zh: 要做到 24 小时不间断运转，我这个团队大概需要 11 个人，而且他们不只是处理项目，还要处理针对已发布项目的违规举报、申诉，以及其他一系列事务。

turns.en: And in the space of about two sessions of half an hour to an hour, you can now completely automate that queue processing. So what I mean by that is you can have an AI go in there, pick up things that the human would normally process in the queue.
turns.zh: 而现在，只要两三次半小时到一小时的会话，你就能把这个队列处理完全自动化。我的意思是，你可以让 AI 进去，接手原本由人在队列里处理的事项。

turns.en: The human might take out in the five, three, five minutes to process that item. AI can do that a lot quicker, reliably 24 by 7. And all of a sudden, the queue is completely automated.
turns.zh: 人处理一项可能要三到五分钟，AI 能做得快得多，还能可靠地 24 小时运转。突然之间，整个队列就完全自动化了。

turns.en: And I had the other day a performance marker to quit on me. That's a fairly expensive role. It's a six figure role in the order of $150,000, $200,000.
turns.zh: 前几天，我这儿一位做效果营销（performance marketing）的员工辞职了。这是个挺贵的岗位，六位数薪水，大概 15 万到 20 万美元。

turns.en: I guess if you're out in the market trying to replace that role. And what do they do every day? They have a very repeatable role, which is they look into Google ads every day.
turns.zh: 如果你想市场上再招一个人来顶这个岗位的话。他们每天做什么呢？其实是一个非常重复性的岗位——每天看 Google Ads。

turns.en: They look through the dashboard graphs, performance on the site. They literally look for all your different ad campaigns and they figure out what should they tune today, should they shift a little bit of budget from one portfolio of ads to another portfolio of ads, et cetera.
turns.zh: 他们看仪表盘上的图表、网站的表现，一个个去看你所有的广告投放活动，判断今天该调什么，是不是该把一点预算从一个广告组合挪到另一个广告组合，诸如此类。

turns.en: And really, it's a fairly repetitive role in many circumstances, tuning knobs and dials. And as that person left, I thought to myself, for the first time, I should really learn how AdWords works because we spend an order of half a million dollars a month on this.
turns.zh: 其实在很多情况下，这是个相当重复的岗位，就是不停调各种旋钮和参数。这个人离职的时候，我第一次意识到，我真的应该学一学 AdWords 是怎么运作的，因为我们每个月在这上面要花大概 50 万美元。

turns.en: So I thought I'm going to replace the role. I really should understand how it works. So I jumped in and I was using Claude to tell me which reports to download and explain the interface inside Google ads and so forth and cutting and pasting bits and bobs back and forwards to Claude and uploading CSVs and so forth and getting a handle for how it worked.
turns.zh: 所以我想，我要替代这个岗位，就必须真的搞明白它是怎么运作的。于是我就上手，让 Claude 告诉我该下载哪些报表、解释 Google Ads 里的界面等等，然后各种复制粘贴给 Claude、上传 CSV 之类的，慢慢摸清它是怎么运作的。

turns.en: And then I had a breakthrough moment where I was like, you know, I could probably get an agent to do this. And every day, before I get into work, look through everything, look through our Google Analytics, look through our Google Ads account, look through our database, look through our financial performance in the last 24 hours, look through the code, look through what's been shipped, look through Fabricator, which is the ticketing system
turns.zh: 然后我突然灵光一现——我大概可以让一个 agent 来做这件事：每天在我到公司之前，把所有东西过一遍：看我们的 Google Analytics、看我们的 Google Ads 账户、看我们的数据库、看过去 24 小时的财务表现、看代码、看已经上线的功能、看 Fabricator（我们的工单系统）——

turns.en: and basically provide a comprehensive report in my email every morning, reliably, when I come in, that will tell me how I should modify the Ads account.
turns.zh: 然后每天早上稳定地把一份综合报告发到我邮箱里，等我到公司的时候，它已经告诉我该如何调整 Ads 账户。

turns.en: And it does it at a superhuman level because it has access to all that data and reviews of that data. And no human, no matter how much I looked into the market to find someone great, there's no way that they'll be getting up every morning at 4am and producing a report by 4.10 for landing in my inbox to make sure when I come to work in the morning, it's there.
turns.zh: 而且它做得比人还厉害，因为它能访问所有那些数据以及对这些数据的复盘。不管我在市场上找多优秀的人，都不可能有人每天早上 4 点起床、4 点 10 分就把报告放进我收件箱，让我一到公司就能看到。

turns.en: I don't want to replace that role, a technical specialist in performance marketing. I'd rather hire someone maybe a little bit more marketing orientated or think down funnel in the whole flow of the customer journey.
turns.zh: 我不想再补招效果营销技术专家这个岗位了。我更愿意招一个更偏营销导向的人，能从整个客户旅程的角度去想漏斗下游的问题。

turns.en: And in the last couple of weeks in particular, I have been going through team by team, looking at which teams are basically queue processes, i.e. they come in the morning and there's a whole bunch of things queued up for them to do, whether it's Amazon data or processor report or whatever it may be, and sit down with the team leaders and basically automate that flow.
turns.zh: 特别是过去这两周，我一直在一个团队一个团队地过，看哪些团队基本上就是队列处理——也就是他们早上一来，就有一堆排队的事情等着做，不管是 Amazon 数据、处理商报告还是别的什么——然后和团队 leader 坐下来，把这个流程自动化掉。

turns.en: And the speed at which you can do it is absolutely phenomenal. For 17 years, I've tried to have my team produce a daily report in the morning by 9.30am in their time zone.
turns.zh: 你能做到的速度绝对惊人。整整 17 年，我都在试图让团队每天早上按他们所在时区 9 点半之前给我出一份日报。

turns.en: And for 17 years, I don't get it at 9.30, I get it maybe at 11 o'clock in the day, 2pm, or maybe they forget to do it. And now I've got AI producing that report and reports with basically every team about what I did in the last time period, how that's tracking if they ship something to production, etc. and so forth.
turns.zh: 17 年来，我从来不是 9 点半收到，而是 11 点、下午 2 点，或者他们干脆忘了做。现在我有 AI 来生成这份报告，而且几乎每个团队都有——报告上一个时段做了什么、进展如何、有没有把什么东西推到生产环境等等。

turns.en: And this is really just lifting the productivity across the board and it's achieving insights into my company that I've never been able to achieve before reliably at a superhuman level.
turns.zh: 这真的在全面提升生产力，让我获得了以前根本无法稳定获得的、对我公司的洞察力，而且是超人级别的。

turns.en: Now, all of that, I'm sure, was covered in just a single $20 per month anthropic subscription to Claude. No, so I mean, therein lies the rub.
turns.zh: 我猜，所有这一切都包含在你每月 20 美元的 Anthropic Claude 订阅里了吧？不，问题就在这里。

turns.en: So I went and looked at my open router token usage for that day and it came in at one particular day last week and it came in at four billion tokens in one day.
turns.zh: 我去查了一下自己那一天在 OpenRouter 上的 token 用量，上周某一天，一天下来是 40 亿 token。

turns.en: And that's four billion with a B. Now, I looked at that and I thought to myself, Jesus, I mean, that cost me about $1,300. That cost me about $1,300 US dollars.
turns.zh: 是 40 亿（4 billion）那个 B。我看着这个数字心想，天呐，这花了我大约 1300 美元——大概 1300 美元。

turns.en: Now, I was using Western models. I mean, $900 was Sonnet, anthropic Sonnet model, which is a cheaper, faster model. There was a little bit of fable in there for doing things like writing effective tickets to feed into our AI software engineering team because we've got a thing called DFID, which will process tickets now and actually do the engineering.
turns.zh: 我用的是西方模型。其中 900 美元是 Sonnet，也就是 Anthropic 的 Sonnet 模型，比较便宜也比较快。里面还有一点 Fable，用来做一些事情，比如写有效的工单，喂给我们的 AI 软件工程团队——因为我们有一个叫 DFID 的东西，它现在会处理工单，然后真的去做工程实现。

turns.en: There's a bit of grok in there, etc., but it was at $1,300. And I thought to myself, Jesus, this is adding huge amounts of value to my company, but I'm only just getting started and at $1,300 US dollars.
turns.zh: 里面也有一点 Grok 等等，但总量就是 1300 美元。我心里想，天呐，这给我公司带来了巨大的价值，但我才刚刚开始，就已经是 1300 美元。

turns.en: I mean, I can imagine going from 40 agents to 400 agents in no time. And all of a sudden, that becomes a $13,000 bill a day. And I could probably even notice her to the end of that in terms of the usage.
turns.zh: 我能想象从 40 个 agent 扩到 400 个 agent 只是转眼之间的事。突然之间，就变成一天 13000 美元的账单，而且我可能连用量天花板都摸不到。

turns.en: So the first thing that starts coming to us in my mind is, well, how can I cut the cost? Hang on. Let me pause you just for one second there because I do want to understand this in perspective.
turns.zh: 所以我脑子里冒出来的第一个念头就是：好，我怎么把成本压下来？等一下，让我打断你一秒钟，因为我真的想把这个事情放到一个更宽的视角里理解一下。

turns.en: I heard you say to me off the air the other day, you know, oh my God, $1,300 in tokens in one day. We're used to getting free stuff on the internet, but you also told me in this conversation so far that you had just one of the employees who used to do this stuff for you, $200,000 a year position.
turns.zh: 前几天你在录制之外跟我说，天呐，一天光 token 就 1300 美元。我们习惯了从互联网上白拿东西，但你在这段对话里也告诉我，你原来光是有一个员工做这些事，就是年薪 20 万美元的岗位。

turns.en: So that's $800 a day right there. You're spending a half a million a month on AdWords. If somebody just optimizes that to save 10% of that, that's worth, by my calculations, about $1,700 a day.
turns.zh: 所以光那一个岗位就是每天 800 美元。你一个月在 AdWords 上花 50 万美元。如果有人只是把它优化到省下 10%，按我算大概就值每天 1700 美元。

turns.en: So you're up to $2,500 a day just right there before doing anything else. This is much bigger than getting free stuff on the internet, but it sounds like it's kind of worth it.
turns.zh: 所以什么都还没做，你光这两项加起来就已经是每天 2500 美元了。这可比"在互联网上白拿东西"大得多，但听起来还是挺值的。

turns.en: It certainly is, but then you start thinking to yourself, well, I'm going to 10x this, you know, because that's all the work I did last month.
turns.zh: 确实很值，但接着你就会想，好，我还要把这个搞成 10 倍——因为那还只是我上个月做的工作。

turns.en: What's going to happen next month? And then you're also thinking about, well, how's pricing going to head in the future and are they going to escalate prices?
turns.zh: 下个月会怎么样？然后你还会想，未来价格会往哪个方向走，他们会不会涨价？

turns.en: And we can talk about that a little bit later in the show. But the first thing you're thinking of, well, that's a month's worth of work getting that fleet up and running.
turns.zh: 这个我们节目后面可以再聊。但你想的第一件事是：好，把这支 agent 队伍搭起来并跑通，就是一个月的工作量。

turns.en: And yes, there's some optimizations you can do. And it turns out that $4 billion of token burn in a day wasn't really $4 billion in a sense in that these models today now have what's called prompt caching.
turns.zh: 是的，你可以做一些优化。而且事实证明，一天 40 亿 token 的消耗在某种意义上并不真的是 40 亿——因为现在的模型都有所谓的 prompt caching（提示缓存）。

turns.en: When you do a genetic work, what you're doing is a lot of these agencies are just going in loops. So for every hour, they might be checking a queue or every hour, they might be, you know, scanning something or checking the database or what have you.
turns.zh: 当你做 agentic 工作时，很多 agent 其实就是在循环里跑。可能每小时检查一次队列，或者每小时扫点什么、看看数据库等等。

turns.en: So there's a lot of tokens that kind of just get reused in the models. And so it turned out with my $4 billion of tokens I spent in that day, $3 billion of them were actually in the prompt caching.
turns.zh: 所以有大量 token 其实在模型里是被反复复用的。结果就是，我那天烧掉的 40 亿 token 里，有 30 亿实际上是走了 prompt caching。

turns.en: If that was not the case, and I was using an opus level model, it would have been probably $80,000 worth of spend. But, you know, I was using a low grade model and there's a lot of caching going on.
turns.zh: 如果没有缓存、我又用的是 Opus 级别的模型，那大概会是 8 万美元的开销。但我用的是低端模型，而且缓存帮了大忙。

turns.en: And it also turns out my code wasn't very efficient, right? So the next thing that came along was I kind of looked at and thought, okay, it's not, yeah, a few of these things I can, that I'm doing around the polling and so forth, I can actually push into software.
turns.zh: 而且我的代码其实也不够高效。接下来我看了看，心想，好，我做的这些轮询之类的东西，其实可以下沉到软件里去做。

turns.en: The neat thing is with AI is you can write a prompt saying, please optimize yourself for costs and take a little bit of your token usage, et cetera, and try and reduce it.
turns.zh: AI 有意思的一点是，你可以直接写一个 prompt 说：请针对成本优化你自己，看看你的 token 用量等等，试着把它降下来。

turns.en: So it turned out that by just typing in that one single prompt, I managed to optimize the token usage down by another 85%. Still, if you kind of think about it intuitively, you know, that was $1,300 of spend.
turns.zh: 结果就是，光是打了这一个 prompt，我就把 token 用量又优化下去了 85%。不过直观想一想，那还是 1300 美元的开销。

turns.zh: 我发誓我不是编的、也不是夸张。有一天上午晚些时候，我正在心里对自己说这段话。我琢磨着该吃午饭了，就跳上电梯下楼去买个三明治。结果在电梯里碰到我们大楼的维修工 Pete，人特别好。Pete 就是那个修水管、灯泡坏了换灯泡的人。蓝领，人非常好，我认识他有几年了。

turns.en: Usually when I talked to him, my conversation was about his Jeep. He really liked his Jeep. But I noticed he sold his Jeep and he seemed to have a new truck. So I thought, Pete, what's you up to? How's your week? A winter ago, he says, boy, you know, I'll tell you, I am absolutely loving Claude Code. All these years I've been using the internet, I thought it was just websites.
turns.zh: 通常我跟他聊天都是聊他的 Jeep，他非常喜欢他的 Jeep。但我注意到他把 Jeep 卖了，好像换了辆新皮卡。所以我就问："Pete，最近忙什么？这周怎么样？"他跟我说："老兄，你知道吗，我告诉你，我完全爱上 Claude Code 了。这么多年我用互联网，我一直以为它就是些网站。"

turns.en: I didn't know about APIs. I didn't know you could write your own code to actually script APIs on different servers to do different things and develop your own dashboards. It's really cool.
turns.zh: "我以前不知道有 API，也不知道你可以自己写代码去调用不同服务器上的 API 来做各种事，还能开发自己的仪表盘。真的太酷了。"

turns.en: I'm really enjoying it. It's this guy's hobby. He's a maintenance guy and he figured it all out because someone who is an above average, smarter than the average blue collar handyman who's curious about how things work and willing to spend a little bit of time investigating and self teaching with no help is able to figure out how to write AI agents that talk to APIs.
turns.zh: "我玩得很开心。"这就是这个人的爱好。他是个维修工，全靠自己琢磨出来——一个比一般蓝领维修工更聪明一点、对事物运作方式好奇、愿意花点时间自己研究、没人教也自学的人，就能琢磨出怎么写跟 API 对话的 AI agent。

turns.en: Whoa, that says to me that this whole thing can happen way faster with far less specialized human skill than I ever imagined. The AI writes the code now, right? So we went from machine code to a higher level language, assembly language to compiled languages like C to interpreted languages.
turns.zh: 哇，这告诉我：整件事发生的速度可能远比我想象的更快，所需要的专业人类技能也远比我想象的更少。现在是 AI 在写代码，对吧？所以我们从机器码走到更高级的语言，从汇编语言走到 C 这样的编译型语言，再走到解释型语言。

turns.en: And now we've basically moved to English. I don't write code anymore. I use my phone and in the chat, the agentic chat harness, you know, I use Py remote, but you can use, I literally just write English.
turns.zh: 而现在我们基本上已经切换到英语了。我不再自己写代码。我用手机，在聊天里、在 agentic 聊天 harness 里——你知道，我用 Py remote，但你也可以用别的——我字面意义上就是写英语。

turns.en: And so someone like the maintenance man can literally say, I want to create a dashboard. I want it to show the following things, put it together and the AI might say, okay, I need an API to this and API to that. And really what you do is you log into these sites, you get the key, which is like a password, you know, which is the API, you know, to access the API, you provide it to the AI and all of a sudden the dashboard's made. And you really see a progression of this sort of
turns.zh: 所以像那个维修工这样的人，真的可以直接说："我想做一个仪表盘，我想让它显示下面这些东西，你把它拼出来。"AI 可能会说："好，我需要访问这个的 API、访问那个的 API。"你要做的就是登录这些网站，拿到 key（就像密码一样，用来访问 API 的），把它交给 AI，突然之间仪表盘就做好了。你真的能看到这种

turns.en: agentic work when I see people get red-pilled in my company that they start off, they start making a dashboard so they can make the job more efficient. So for example, my ops team in load shift has it, which is, you know, maybe have a hell of a trait. They have a dashboard that says, okay, you got to call this guy in the next two minutes. You know, this is a particular custom that's blowing up at the moment. Here's your next activity to do, et cetera. Here's here,
turns.zh: agentic 工作的进阶——我看到公司里的人被"red-pill"之后，一开始是做一个仪表盘让工作更高效。比如我在 Loadshift 的运营团队就有——那可能是一份苦差事——他们有一个仪表盘说："好，你得在未来两分钟内给这个人打电话。你知道，这是一个正在爆单的特定客户。你的下一个动作是什么什么，等等。""

turns.en: tracking towards your commissions, your hurdles, your accelerator, a few commissions and so on. So everything they need is in that dashboard. And in fact, the team leader wrote it, is they can give feedback to the dashboard to improve it. So it has a little chat, little box in the side, they can just type in a bit of feedback and bang the dashboard update itself. So you can make dashboards very easy, you can make reports very easy. So as I mentioned
turns.zh: "还有你离佣金、门槛、佣金加速器还差多少等等。"所以他们需要的一切都在这个仪表盘里。而且事实上，团队 leader 写这个仪表盘的时候，还让他们可以给仪表盘反馈来改进它。旁边有一个小的聊天框，他们直接输入一点反馈，砰，仪表盘自己就更新了。所以做仪表盘很容易，做报告也很容易。就像我

turns.en: before, every morning, I have a report around my ads program and what I should do and what knobs and dials I should process. But then you move to the next level, which is queue processing. So, you know, that report says here's an extra few action items to take ticking through those action items, you can get our to do that. Many businesses have queues already, you know, they might have a support ticket queue, or a support chat queue, or what have you, you know, AI now does 100% of our
turns.zh: 之前提到的，每天早上我都会收到一份关于我的广告计划的报告，告诉我该做什么、该调哪些旋钮和参数。但接着你会走向下一个层级，也就是队列处理。那份报告会说：这几个额外的 action item 你去勾一勾，你可以让 AI 去做。很多企业本来就有队列——支持工单队列、支持聊天队列等等——你知道，现在 AI 已经处理我们

turns.en: tier one interactions with customers. And the advantage there is that you get instant response 24 by seven any language you like, the answers are four times longer, four times better and 10 times more empathetic, at a level of empathy that is no support person, the world could sustain over a 24 hour period. And yes, a lot of stuff gets escalated to humans. And then the human comes in and has to do what have you. But increasingly, that's going to be less likely case.
turns.zh: 100% 的一线客户交互。好处是：即时响应、24 小时、任何语言都可以；答案长度是原来的 4 倍、质量是原来的 4 倍、共情是原来的 10 倍——那种共情程度是世界上任何客服人员都无法在 24 小时里持续保持的。是的，很多东西还是会被升级给人类，然后人类进来要做这做那。但这种情形会越来越少。

turns.en: And, you know, ultimately, I think there's going to be a massive transformation. I mean, if you think about jobs in big companies, right, I mean, we've talked about before, how anywhere there's a large number of people doing the same thing over and over and over again, you know, you might have your 100 lawyers, junior lawyers doing drafting a law firm in the future, you might not need 100, you might need 13, you know, 10,000 people on the call center,
turns.zh: 你知道，最终我觉得会有一场大规模转型。想想大公司里的岗位——我们之前也聊过——凡是有大量人反复做同一件事的地方：一家律所未来可能不需要 100 个初级律师做起草，可能只要 13 个；呼叫中心 1 万人，

turns.en: you might need 100 or 200, what have you. I mean, this is this is now taking that to the next level because the AI now is getting quite reliable for what's called a genetic use, which means that they can have long loops and get to quite complicated things over a period of time and so forth without drifting. Admittedly, some of the Chinese models do have a bit of a struggle sometimes with things like tool use and so on deep six and sometimes it's going to a little bit of a loop,
turns.zh: 可能只要 100 到 200 人。也就是说，现在这件事正在被推向下一个层级，因为 AI 在所谓的 agentic 使用上已经变得相当可靠——它可以跑长循环、在一段时间里处理相当复杂的事情而不跑偏。诚然，一些中国模型在 tool use 之类的东西上有时会有点吃力，DeepSeek 有时候会陷进一个小循环，

turns.en: but that's more of an engineering problem around the harness. I mean, that's why you kind of pale a bit more for the anthropic models because they do have an advantage in the sort of genetic work for now, but that's being eroded quite rapidly. But what it basically means is, I mean, what business wouldn't want to have something that logs into all your databases or your web traffic or have you look through your customer interactions and just tells you what's going on in your business
turns.zh: 但那更多是 harness 层的工程问题。所以你会更愿意为 Anthropic 的模型多掏点钱，因为眼下他们在 agentic 工作上确实有优势，不过这个优势正在被非常快地侵蚀。这基本上意味着——哪个企业会不想有一个东西，能登录你所有的数据库、你的网站流量，或者翻看你所有的客户交互，然后每天告诉你你的业务在发生什么、

turns.en: every day and tells you where the opportunities are and tells you where the weaknesses are and tells all the humans what they should be doing next in the most optimal order that they do the next thing and free you up from a lot of this work to focus on the creative, the really high value-adding, etc. work. And frankly, no human can compete anymore with some of these tasks.
turns.zh: 机会在哪里、弱点在哪里，并以最优的顺序告诉所有人下一步该做什么，把你从大量这类工作里解放出来，让你去专注创造性、真正高附加值的工作？坦白讲，很多这类任务，人类已经竞争不过了。

turns.en: Like the ability to issue a report from an AI agent, it's far superior to any human. It's superhuman already because no human would ever get up in the morning at 4, 5, 6 a.m. review what needed to be reviewed in the time period to issue the report and do it so with a level of consistency day in, day out, every single day of the year, it's impossible to do that.
turns.zh: 比如让一个 AI agent 出报告的能力，已经远远超过任何人类。它已经是超人级别了——因为没有人会每天早上 4 点、5 点、6 点起床，把这段时间需要复盘的东西都过一遍再出报告，还能一年 365 天、天天如此、保持一致，这根本不可能。

turns.en: So I think there's going to be tremendous dislocation in the corporate world. I mean, I wouldn't want to be a long commercial real estate at the moment. It's not because the work from mine is because the AI is going to chew through a lot of these jobs and it's going to chew through a lot of the, you know, every business if you're a banker, one of our big banks in Australia has got 50,000 employees and 700 branches and you kind of think to yourself,
turns.zh: 所以我觉得企业世界会出现巨大的错位。我可不想现在做多商业地产——不是因为居家办公，而是因为 AI 会嚼掉大量这类岗位，会嚼掉大量——你知道，每个行业都是这样。如果你是银行，我们澳大利亚一家大银行有 5 万名员工、700 家分行，你会想：

turns.en: what are those people doing? You don't need to do 50,000 people that run 700 branches. You know, what are the workflows inside a bank? You've got to approve mortgage applications.
turns.zh: 这些人到底在做什么？你不需要 5 万人来运营 700 家分行。银行内部都有哪些工作流？你要审批房贷申请，

turns.en: It's probably a queue of them. You've got to do your credit checks and AML checks. What else are you going to do? Put a few faces at the tellers to make people think you're still a friendly bank, but you could probably run that entire bank, not with 50,000 people. You could run it with certainly 10,000 people and certainly probably a lot less than that. So you're going to get a lot of dislocation now coming through. Where does it head? If it's thinking more about
turns.zh: 这大概是一个队列。你要做信用检查、AML（反洗钱）检查。你还能做什么？在柜台上摆几张脸，让人们觉得你还是一家友好的银行——但整个银行你其实不需要 5 万人来运营，1 万人肯定够，甚至可能远远少于 1 万人。所以接下来会出现大量错位。它会走向哪里？如果更多地思考

turns.en: the product design, the architecture and so forth, so they're moving up the stack. And perhaps a lot of the illustrators now are not really pushing pixels around the screen, they're thinking more like a creative director. Where do we end? I think we end in an explosion of entrepreneurship. I think we end in a hyper competitive, very entrepreneurial society and I kind of think to, you know, where's one of the most competitive markets in the world for
turns.zh: 产品设计、架构等等，那么他们就是在往栈的上面走。也许很多插画师现在不再是在屏幕上推像素，而是更像创意总监那样思考。最终我们会走到哪里？我觉得我们会走到一场创业大爆炸。我觉得我们会走到一个超级竞争、非常有创业精神的社会。我会想：世界上这类事情最激烈的市场之一在哪里？

turns.en: this sort of thing? You think about India. You go to India and there's a lot of people who are not in traditional employment who have to kind of fend for themselves and kind of what do you end up?
turns.zh: 你会想到印度。你去印度，那儿有很多人并不在传统雇佣关系里，必须自己谋生。结果是什么？

turns.en: Everyone's got a hustle. One guy's making food at a store, one guy's repairing motorcycle seats, one guy's doing a tour guide, et cetera. Maybe they're doing a few different things, et cetera.
turns.zh: 每个人都有自己的 hustle（副业/谋生手段）。有人在店里做吃的，有人在修摩托车座，有人在做导游等等，可能一个人还同时做好几件事。

turns.en: I think that's going to happen in the Western world. You're kind of seeing already the people having hustles doing, you know, UGC content or maybe they're buying poker online or, you know, they've got drop shipping business or selling courses or whatever it may be. And I just think playing with prediction markets, whatever it may be, vibe coding apps and so on. And I think that's kind of where we head is we stand up in this world where you're going to have, you know,
turns.zh: 我觉得西方世界也会变成这样。你现在已经能看到有人在搞副业，做 UGC 内容，或者在网上打扑克，或者做 dropshipping、卖课程等等。我觉得还有玩预测市场、vibe coding 做 app 之类。我觉得这就是我们要走到的地方：我们站起来，进入这样一个世界，

turns.en: just everybody's going to have a hustle, everybody's going to run a startup or a business, et cetera. We've had this point since human history where you've had technology get to a point where it's created such productivity breakthroughs that you have dislocations. So you've got the mechanization of agriculture, you know, that day that someone drives the tractor onto the farm and there's 1,000 people on the farm and you don't get 1,000 people anymore, you need 20. You've got the
turns.zh: 每个人都会有自己的 hustle，每个人都会开一家创业公司或者一门生意等等。人类历史上一直有这样的时刻：技术发展到一个节点，创造出巨大的生产力突破，从而带来错位。比如农业机械化——那一天有人把拖拉机开进农场，原本农场有 1000 个人，从此你不再需要 1000 个人，你只需要 20 个。你还会有

turns.en: mechanization of the factory. You've got the computerization of white collar jobs with the transistor and the computer and then the internet and mobile. And now you've got AI, which is really going to do it to white collar jobs. And, you know, there's going to be in the future, there'll be jobs thought of that we never might today be fanciful if we imagined it. I can imagine that 100 years ago, you tried to describe someone that produced memes or UGC content. I probably think
turns.zh: 工厂的机械化，你还会有晶体管、计算机、然后互联网和移动化带来的白领岗位信息化。现在你有了 AI，它真的要冲着白领岗位来了。未来会有一些今天听起来天马行空的岗位。我可以想象，100 年前你要跟人描述一个专门做 meme 或者 UGC 内容的人，别人大概会觉得

turns.en: this is a ridiculous job, but those jobs kind of exist today. But we are going to go through a tremendous dislocation now on white collar jobs. Let's go a little deeper on that white collar job dislocation in terms of how it plays out over time. Because if you talk about the long term, this seems really clear to me, people whining about losing their jobs. Look, AI is an incredible productivity tool. If you take the blue collar physical labor equivalent before the industrial
turns.zh: 这是个荒唐的岗位，但这些岗位今天真的存在。不过我们现在真的会在白领岗位上经历一场巨大的错位。让我们再深入聊聊白领岗位错位随时间会怎么演化。因为如果你谈长期，这一点在我看来非常清楚——人们抱怨失去工作。听着，AI 是一个不可思议的生产力工具。拿工业革命前蓝领体力劳动的等价物来看，

turns.en: revolution, it took hundreds of men with picks and shovels to clear an acre. Now one guy on a big caterpillar earth moving machine can do it in a half an hour because we have much more productivity thanks to automation. AI is the same thing for white collar, you know, it's much better that we have a world where the blue collar guy can drive a machine instead of having to break his back with a pickaxe. That's better. But wait a minute, if you were one of the thousand guys
turns.zh: 开垦一英亩地需要几百个人拿着镐和铲子。现在一个人开着大型 Caterpillar 推土机半小时就能干完，因为自动化带来了大得多的生产力。AI 对白领来说是一样的道理。你知道，一个蓝领工人能开机器而不是靠镐头累断腰，这个世界当然更好。但等一下——如果你就是那 1000 个

turns.en: that got let go on the day that that first tractor got delivered and not the one guy that got, you know, kept to drive it, you're not feeling good about that. Maybe your kids are going to love the fact that they're growing up in a new, better world, but it's going to suck for you for a while.
turns.zh: 在第一台拖拉机交付那天被裁掉的人中的一个，而不是被留下来开它的那一个，你的感觉可不会好。也许你的孩子会喜欢自己成长在一个新的、更好的世界，但对你来说，一段时间里日子会很难熬。

turns.en: Seems to me like AI is an incredible productivity tool for white collar, except for the people that kind of are hanging around when it shows up. What do we do about that?
turns.zh: 在我看来，AI 是白领生产力上不可思议的工具，除了对那些恰好在它出现时还挂在岗位上的人。这个我们该怎么办？

turns.en: Yeah, I think about for a slightly different perspective at the same time. Someone asked me, you know, what do you tell your kids? Should they go to uni? Like, what skills do you need to survive in this world? If you are laid off because you work at a banker insurance company and all of a sudden they don't need 50,000 staff, they need 5,000, you're laid off. Who's going to swim? Who's going to sink? What happens in that world? And I kind of, when I kind of see what's
turns.zh: 是的，同一时间我也会从一个稍微不同的角度去想。有人问我："你会怎么跟你孩子说？他们该不该上大学？在这个世界里生存需要什么样的技能？"如果你所在的银行或保险公司突然不再需要 5 万员工、只需要 5000 人，你被裁了——谁能浮起来、谁会沉下去？那个世界会发生什么？当我看到我公司里正在

turns.en: happening in my company, people who survive in that world and do really well are people with initiative. You need to be flexible. You need to be dynamic. I think there's a whole bunch of people in my company who are completely red-pilled. You're seeing them watching what they're doing and they're writing agents to kind of automate because this whole technology explosion is essentially about automation. There's automation of the farm, automation of the factory, automation of
turns.zh: 发生的事情时，我觉得能在那个世界里活下来并且做得很好的人，都是有主动性（initiative）的人。你要灵活，你要有活力。我公司里有一大批人已经彻底被 red-pill 了。你看他们在做什么，他们在写 agent 来做自动化，因为整场技术爆炸本质上就是自动化——农业的自动化、工厂的自动化、

turns.en: knowledge jobs, etc. So they get excited and they kind of come with always different roles in automation. They have teams underneath them. One thing that's kind of interesting is I find now that where I've had a functional team before, for example, processing a queue where there might be a team leader and there might be, you know, five people underneath them. Moving forward, it'll be just the team leader and the AI. You don't need the five people underneath them. It would be the
turns.zh: 知识型岗位等等。所以他们很兴奋，他们总会带着自动化的不同角色出现，手下带着团队。有一件有意思的事情是，我发现以前我有个职能团队，比如处理一个队列，可能有一个 team leader、下面带 5 个人。往后就会变成：只有 team leader 加 AI，你不再需要下面那 5 个人。就是

turns.en: team leader controlling the AI and the AI will be the team effectively. And the team leaders, they're kind of coming up with new ideas and kind of directing it and so forth. So it's the people with initiative. It's the people who are very creative. It's the ideas people because the ability now for you to execute an idea is very, very simple. I mean, over the weekend, I've vibrated a whole app for my girlfriend for a birthday coming up around fitness. And it's just amazing
turns.zh: team leader 控制 AI，AI 实际上就是团队。Team leader 不停想出新点子，指挥 AI 去做。所以关键是有主动性的人、非常有创造力的人、有想法的人，因为现在你执行一个想法的能力已经变得非常非常简单。我这个周末就 vibe coding 出了整个一个 app，是给我女朋友的生日礼物，主题是健身。真的令人惊叹，

turns.en: just how quickly you can put some of these things together. So if you just got the idea and you got the initiative, now the execution is there. So they're in there doing all that.

turns.en: His entire thesis is about accelerating AI adoption, but having a strong structural thesis doesn't automatically mean it is a perfect tactical entry right now. And that's why I wanted to express the view through NVIDIA options rather than the shares themselves. January, 2027, option implied volatilities have collapsed towards the lowest levels in the past year, which means the cost of owning optionality is about as cheap as we've seen over that period.
turns.zh: 他整个 thesis 就是 AI 采用在加速，但有一个强的结构性 thesis 并不自动意味着现在就是完美的战术入场点。这就是为什么我想通过 NVIDIA 期权、而不是股票本身来表达这个观点。2027 年 1 月到期的期权隐含波动率已经塌到过去一年的最低位附近，这意味着拥有 optionality（可选性）的成本大概是这段时间里最便宜的水平。

turns.en: So rather than taking full Delta 1 exposure in the stock, I'd rather use that relatively inexpensive volatility to buy defined risk upside convexity. With NVIDIA trading around $224.31 at the time of this recording, I'm looking at the January 15th, 2027, $125 strike call, which is essentially at the money and gives us 128 days till the expiration. The call is trading around $21.60 or just under 10% of the value of the stock with an implied volatility around 38%.
turns.zh: 所以与其在股票上拿一个完整的 Delta 1 敞口，我更愿意用这个相对便宜的波动率去买一个定义风险的上行 convexity（凸性）。录制这期时 NVIDIA 交易价大概在 224.31 美元，我看的是 2027 年 1 月 15 日到期、行权价 125 美元的 call，基本上是平价期权（at the money），距离到期还有 128 天。这个 call 交易价大概 21.60 美元，也就是股票价值的不到 10%，隐含波动率大概 38%。

turns.en: The attraction to expressing the trade this way is flexibility. If NVIDIA corrects into the midterms, the call gives us the defined risk, downside Delta compression, and positive Vega if volatility spikes potentially cushioning any drawdown versus owning the shares outright. That preserves capital and most importantly gives us the ability to tactically reposition at lower prices. Alternatively, if NVIDIA breaks to new highs and the semiconductor bull market reaccelerates,
turns.zh: 用这种方式表达交易的吸引力在于灵活性。如果 NVIDIA 在中期选举前回调，这个 call 给我们定义好的下行风险、下行 Delta 压缩，还有正的 Vega——如果波动率飙升，可能会缓冲回撤，相比于直接持有股票。这保住资本，最重要的是给了我们在更低价格上战术性重新布局的能力。反过来，如果 NVIDIA 突破新高、半导体牛市重新加速，

turns.en: we own open-ended upside convexity purchased when volatility was near its cheapest levels in the past year. So the trade is simple, cheap, long-dated optionality, defined downside, positive Vega, and open-ended upside participation. That's where's the trade.
turns.zh: 我们就拥有了一份开放式的上行 convexity，是在过去一年里波动率最便宜的水平附近买进的。所以这笔交易很简单：便宜的、长期限的 optionality，定义好的下行，正的 Vega，还有开放式的上行参与。这就是这周的 trade 所在。

And despite some traders covering those contracts, significant short exposure still remains in this market today. Now with oil surging again this month, how much do you see this move being driven by the fundamentals and how much is
turns.zh: 我们在这个节目上一直在呼吁更高价格，因为持仓长期以来一直偏空。就两个月前，7 月的时候，WTI 的总空头持仓达到了五年极值，接近 24.2 万手合约。尽管一些交易者已经平掉了这些合约，这个市场今天仍然存在显著的空头敞口。这个月油价再次飙升，你觉得这一波有多少是基本面驱动，有多少是

turns.en: a crowded short trade being squeezed? Well, the squeeze is underway, like literally as we're recording, we just printed 100 on WTI. You know, the geopolitical premium has been a physical supply story again. This is not merely just a fear of a disruption, but the disruption is occurring. The global inventory buffer is dangerously thin. The EIA estimated global oil inventories have fallen roughly 400 million barrels and oil is ripping. But the fascinating part
turns.zh: 一场拥挤的空头交易被 squeeze？嗯，squeeze 正在进行——就在我们录制的这一刻，WTI 刚刚触及 100 美元。地缘政治溢价一直是一个实物供给的故事。这不只是对中断的恐惧，而是中断正在发生。全球库存缓冲已经薄到危险的地步。EIA 估计全球石油库存已经下降了大约 4 亿桶，油价正在 ripping。但最有意思的部分是

turns.en: is large speculators that hedge fund community has not been rebuilding their speculative positioning and shorts have stubbornly held on to their positions. So the flows have clearly fuel to drive this with this kind of a rip. This is certainly a disruptor in the markets. And it'll be very interesting to see whether oil sustains above 100 or whether this fades quickly into next week.
turns.zh: 大投机者——对冲基金群体——并没有在重建他们的投机性持仓，而空头一直死守着自己的仓位。所以资金流显然在助推这一波 rip。这绝对是市场里的一个 disruptor（扰乱因素）。看看油价能不能持续在 100 美元以上、还是很快就在下周回落，会非常有意思。

turns.en: Now, when you put all the stuff you were talking about together, so rising oil prices, surging yields, and even renewed inflation risk, how vulnerable does that leave the equity market?
turns.zh: 把你刚才说的这些放到一起——上涨的油价、飙升的收益率、甚至重新升温的通胀风险——这让股市显得多么脆弱？

turns.en: Are we setting up for a meaningful breakdown or are there still enough bullish forces to keep the market together? Well, this is such a fascinating topic because on the surface the markets are absorbing the initial oil and rates pressures. But under the hood, there is a clear structural deterioration. I'd like to think of like an analogy of the castle built on sand and the sand is shifting under the castle, but the castle hasn't yet moved. The puzzle to solve
turns.zh: 我们是在为一场有意义的 breakdown（跌破）做准备，还是仍然有足够多的多头力量把市场撑住？嗯，这是一个非常有意思的话题，因为表面上市场正在吸收最初的油价和利率压力。但在引擎盖下面，有一个明显的结构性恶化。我喜欢用一个类比：一座建在沙子上的城堡，沙子在城堡下面移动，但城堡本身还没有动。要解开的谜题是：

turns.en: is there a strong enough foundation to keep this market elevated or is the deterring market breath going to inevitably crack this market? Now, the first thing to highlight is there's a huge deterioration in that breath. A month ago, we were at 70% of S&P 500 stocks bull trending above their 50 day moving average. Since then, over the last month, we've seen breath collapse to near 35%. That means 50% of those trending stocks all broke down. So why no response in the cash
turns.zh: 有没有一个足够强的基础把市场撑在高位，还是恶化的市场宽度会不可避免地让市场裂开？首先要强调的是市场宽度出现了巨大恶化。一个月前，S&P 500 里有 70% 的股票处在 50 日均线上方的多头趋势里。从那时起，过去一个月我们看到宽度崩塌到接近 35%。也就是说，那些趋势股里有 50% 全都跌破了。那为什么现金

turns.en: index? Because this was accompanied by a pop in a few of the mega cap heavyweights in the Mag7 and semiconductor basket. Sector wise, you see financials have weakened to testing their 50 day moving average. While clear breakdowns have occurred in consumer discretionary space, consumer staples, retailers, industrials, defense contractors, home builders, utilities, transports, REITs, the list goes on. That's counterweighted so far against miners holding up
turns.zh: 指数没有反应？因为这伴随着 Mag7 和半导体篮子里几只超大市值权重股的暴涨。分板块看，金融板块已经弱到在测试它们的 50 日均线；同时消费非必需品、消费必需品、零售、工业、国防承包商、住宅建筑商、公用事业、运输、REITs 都出现了明显的跌破，这个列表还能继续。到目前为止，这些被矿业股保持得

turns.en: pretty well. The energy stocks continue to trend strongly and the biotechs, at least for now, are holding up. But the vulnerability really comes here in the next 100 S&P points. Looking at a lot of the quants like reports from Charlie McKelligan and others that the CTA cell triggers are all around the 7500 to 7550 area, which is just like 50 to 100 S&P points below where we are.
turns.zh: 相当不错所抵消；能源股继续强势 trend，生物科技股至少眼下也顶住了。但真正的脆弱出现在下面 100 点 S&P 的区间里。看很多量化报告——比如 Charlie McElligott（Whisper 记作 McKelligan）等人的报告——CTA 的卖出触发点都在 7500 到 7550 附近，也就是比我们当前位置低 50 到 100 个 S&P 点。

turns.en: Right now, the selling pressure is coming in a little bit, but the question becomes, do we trigger systematic selling flows that can often lead to 100 billion plus in flows pivoting?
turns.zh: 眼下卖压已经开始出来一点，但问题变成：我们会不会触发系统性卖盘资金流，那种往往会带来 1000 亿美元以上资金转向的资金流？

turns.en: We've already seen a substantial pivot in those flows in the Russell, which has already rolled over. Will the S&P join that party? More importantly, will we see things like the semiconductors be able to hold things up if they suddenly start to fall back below their 50-day moving averages? Things get pretty spicy pretty quickly. Let's hone into one of those sectors that were the winning one here over the last few weeks. When you look at gold here and when you
turns.zh: 我们已经看到 Russell 里这些资金流出现了大幅转向，Russell 已经翻下去了。S&P 会不会加入这个 party？更重要的是，如果半导体突然开始跌回 50 日均线下方，我们还能看到它们撑住局面吗？事情会很快变得非常 spicy（火爆）。让我们聚焦到过去几周表现赢家的一个板块上。看看黄金，

turns.en: look at the metal, we've been on a two-year bull trend, but the last six months has been struggling to make further gains. Now, when looking at the COT report, we can see speculative long positioning is rebuilt, but it has not become heavily crowded. Do you see this just as a healthy consolidation within a broader uptrend, or will higher yields keep putting pressure on gold's price?
turns.zh: 看这个金属，我们已经在两年牛市 trend 里，但过去六个月一直在挣扎着继续上涨。看 COT 报告，我们可以看到投机性多头持仓已经重建，但还没有变得非常拥挤。你觉得这只是一个更大上升趋势里健康的盘整，还是更高的收益率会继续压制金价？

turns.en: Well, listen, let's step back and look at gold in the big picture here. First of all, we went through a two-year roaring bull market that ended in January, 2026 with a blowoff up at near 5600.
turns.zh: 嗯，听着，让我们退一步从大局看黄金。首先，我们经历了一波两年的 roaring 牛市，在 2026 年 1 月以接近 5600 的 blowoff up（放量顶）结束。

turns.en: Since then, over the last six months, we have seen a 25% correction in bullion, and fulfilling what a typical market correction would look like. Now, we had a substantial breakout here in the month of August, and now we're backfilling that. Now, from a headwind perspective, obviously, we're seeing real rates rising, but the tailwind is obviously the dollar has weakened, and so it's a situation where there is some positives, some negatives, and we're in
turns.zh: 从那时起，过去六个月我们看到金条出现了 25% 的回调，符合一次典型市场回调的样子。8 月我们有一个大幅突破，现在正在回补那个突破。从逆风的角度看，显然实际利率在上升；但顺风是美元已经走弱。所以这是一个有一些正面、有一些负面的情况，我们处在

turns.en: the middle of a consolidation. Overall, I think gold has genuinely turned the corner. We haven't seen speculators really lean into this in a big way just yet, so it will be very interesting to see whether this gets bought on dip. Overall, it could be a scenario where gold does some consolidation for even a few more months as we maybe grind towards the midterms, but at some stage, I'm leaning that the correction is over and that this gold correction should be bought on
turns.zh: 一次盘整的中间。总的来说，我觉得黄金已经真的转过弯来了。我们还没看到投机者真的大举 lean in，所以看看这个会不会被 buy on dip 会非常有意思。整体来看，可能出现的情景是：黄金再盘整几个月，我们慢慢磨到中期选举，但到某个阶段，我倾向于回调已经结束，这次黄金回调应该被 buy on

turns.en: dip. One thing I want to move on to here, though, Mass, is I wanted to just briefly touch on uranium, because what's interesting is the U308 is actually near $90 now, continues to trend higher.

turns.en: You're seeing general accumulation in uranium, but what's interesting is the uranium miners broke out and seem to continue to correlate with gold miners. Maybe there's an equity basket that includes them together. Not sure how to size that up, but it's clearly been there. Overall, it'll be very interesting to see whether that correlation continues and whether uranium has also turned the corner here and started something more bullish.
turns.zh: 你能看到铀的整体吸筹，但有意思的是铀矿股已经突破，而且似乎继续跟金矿股保持相关。也许有一个把两者都包括在一起的股票篮子。不确定怎么给它定量，但这个相关性明显是存在的。总的来说，看看这种相关性会不会继续、铀是不是也在这里转过弯来、开始更加 bullish 的走势，会非常有意思。

turns.en: For sure, we'll keep watching, but let's turn to the dollar and more importantly, I want to talk about the yen, because we've seen the pair break sharply higher over the past week from both administrations intervening, but the latest caught data still shows large speculators deeply net short this market. Is this simply an intervention-driven squeeze, or could we be seeing the beginning of a much larger yen carry trend unwind going into your end?
turns.zh: 当然，我们会持续关注。但让我们转到美元，更重要的是我想聊聊日元。过去一周我们看到这个货币对因为两国政府干预而急剧向上突破，但最新的 COT 数据仍然显示大投机者深度净空这个市场。这只是一次干预驱动的 squeeze，还是我们可能正在看到一个更大得多的日元 carry 交易 trend 反转的开始？

turns.en: Well, listen, the price action substantially has pivoted over the last month and a half. First of all, it started with that intervention, but the entire correction that happened throughout the remainder of August simply retested the 50-day moving average and was a typical 50% retracement. That decisively broke out. What's really interesting is in the latter part of August, as we saw in those caught reports, actually short sellers came roaring back in. When we get that
turns.zh: 嗯，听着，价格行为在过去一个半月里已经大幅转向。首先，是从那次干预开始的，但整个 8 月余下时间发生的回调只是重新测试了 50 日均线，是一个典型的 50% 回撤，然后决定性地突破了。真正有意思的是，8 月后半段——就像我们在那些 COT 报告里看到的——空头其实 roaring 着回来了。等我们明天拿到那份

turns.en: caught report tomorrow, it'll be very interesting to see how many of them once again got squeezed out of this. What's significant for me is that we've now broken on that yen above their 50-week moving average. Why this is significant is that the yen, basically for almost a year and a half, has been in a decisive downtrend. When we usually get a key breakout like this, it tends to follow through. This is certainly high on my watch list to see whether quick dips in
turns.zh: COT 报告时，看看他们中有多少人再次被 squeeze 出去会非常有意思。对我来说重要的是，日元现在已经突破了 50 周均线。为什么这个重要？因为日元基本上将近一年半一直处于决定性的下降趋势里。当我们通常得到像这样的关键突破时，往往会 follow through（跟进）。这肯定在我的观察名单上排得很靠前——看看日元的快速回调会不会被

turns.en: the yen are being bought and whether we sustain above moving averages and whether a new trend is being established. The fact that the US dollar is generally trending down and weakening is a further support to the idea that the yen can be the strongest currency in this basket.

turns.en: Large speculators in this market were sitting at the 100th percentile on both the one-year and the three-year score. That just means that we've not seen positioning more bullish than this over the last three years. Is this setup dangerous crowding or is the market simply pricing in a deeper tightening supply story? Listen, this isn't just corn. Whether you take wheat, soybeans, sugar, bean oil, or bean meal, we have seen us reach the 100th percentile on one-year
turns.zh: 这个市场里的大投机者在 1 年和 3 年评分上都处在第 100 百分位。这只意味着过去三年我们没见过比这更 bullish 的持仓。这个 setup 是危险的拥挤，还是市场只是在定价一个更深层次的供给收紧故事？听着，这不只是玉米。不管是小麦、大豆、糖、豆油还是豆粕，我们都看到在 1 年

turns.en: and three-year positioning right across the board. When looking at corn specifically on these caught reports, what's interesting is going back a few months, the gross short positioning in corn was almost at a five-year extreme. In the last two months, almost all of those corn shorts have been squeezed. At the same time, the longs have finally come in. We're at a five-year high in gross long positioning and net long positioning. This has genuinely demonstrated crowding,
turns.zh: 和 3 年持仓上全面达到第 100 百分位。具体看玉米的 COT 报告，有意思的是，回到几个月前，玉米的总空头持仓几乎处在五年极值。过去两个月，几乎所有玉米空头都被 squeeze 掉了。同时，多头终于进来了。我们的总多头持仓和净多头持仓都处在五年高点。这真的展示了拥挤，

turns.en: but crowding is not a contrarian trade right off the bat because there is genuine fundamentals behind this. The agricultural complex is repricing supply risk. There's a Ukraine logistic story in there, all sorts of issues with weather like the El Nino. The bottom line is that there's a genuine fundamental reason that these grains are ripping this way. I'm not ready to short this crowded trade, but this is a very well-known and already very well-positioned long position in this space.
turns.zh: 但拥挤并不是一开始就是一个反向交易，因为这背后有真实的基本面。农产品综合体正在重新定价供给风险。里面有乌克兰物流的故事，还有各种各样的天气问题，比如厄尔尼诺。底线是，这些谷物这样 ripping 有一个真实的基本面理由。我还没准备好做空这个拥挤的交易，但这是这个领域里一个非常知名、已经建得非常满的多头仓位。

turns.en: It'll be very interesting to see whether we continue to see the pattern of dips being bought and the bulls keep being rewarded for this long positioning.
